title: Chess with an AI opponent
prompt: Build a complete chess game as a single HTML page in vanilla JavaScript — no libraries; draw the pieces with Unicode chess characters or in code. Enforce all rules: legal move generation with check detection, castling, en passant, pawn promotion with a piece picker, stalemate, checkmate, and draw by insufficient material. Include click-or-drag moving with legal-move highlighting, a minimax AI opponent with alpha-beta pruning searching at least 3 plies with adjustable difficulty, algebraic move notation in a scrollable list, board flip, and an undo button.

A quick introduction

Make your next move

  • Click a piece, then a highlighted square, or drag it there. With a keyboard, use arrows and Enter. Escape clears your selection.
  • Protect your king. A move that leaves it in check is never allowed. Checkmate wins; stalemate draws.
  • To castle, move your king two squares toward its rook. Neither piece may have moved, the path must be clear, and the king cannot cross an attacked square.
  • En passant is available immediately after an opposing pawn advances two squares beside your pawn. A pawn on its final rank promotes to your choice of piece.
  • Insufficient mating material is a draw. You may claim a draw on threefold repetition or after 50 moves by each player without a pawn move or capture. Fivefold repetition and 75 such moves end the game automatically.
  • Undo takes back your last turn against the computer, or one move in Pass & play. Changing sides or modes starts a new game.

The computer uses alpha-beta minimax, completing at least 3 plies. Higher levels search up to 4 or 5 plies within a time budget. A ply is one player's move.
